title: A `#[Core\Json\Derive]` class with no written constructor compiles and gets no codec.
text:
`#[Core\Json\Derive] class P { public int $k = 1; }` passes `nvs check`, and both `Core\Json::encode(new P())` and `Core\Json::decodeAs

(…)` throw `LogicError` "has no JSON codec" at run time. `check_constructor_parameter` returns `None` when the class has no constructor, on the reasoning that `ctor_init` has already reported the unassigned properties; a property with a default is never reported there, so nothing is reported and the field is dropped. With an empty written `constructor()` the same class is `E0460`, as `rule:core-classes/derive-field-list` says. It closes when a deriving class without a constructor is a checker error (or derives a codec whose decoder sets each field), with a conformance case.
